claims: In the long-wavelength limit qr << 1, the multipole radiation field yields decay rate T(sigma lambda) proportional to reduced transition probability B(sigma lambda) with explicit numerical conversion factors for E1-E4 and M1-M4.

Weisskopf single-particle units B_W(E lambda) and B_W(M lambda) derived from an idealized single-particle transition in a rigid sphere of radius R = 1.2 A^(1/3) fm provide model-independent collective enhancement benchmarks.

The single-proton quadrupole moment Qsp = -[(2j-1)/(2j+2)] <r^2> exhibits an equatorial charge concentration for m=j, while a single-proton hole state has Qhole = -Qsp due to particle-hole conjugation.
Core polarization by valence nucleons via virtual coupling to the high-lying 2 hbar omega_0 isoscalar giant quadrupole resonance induces effective charges e_eff(p) ~ 1.5e and e_eff(n) ~ 0.5e.

Single-particle magnetic dipole moments follow the two Schmidt limits for j = l +/- 1/2, and single-particle M1 transitions are strictly forbidden across different orbital angular momentum states (delta l = 0), occurring solely between spin-orbit partners.
